description: A microcontroller board built around the ATmega328P, with 14 digital I/O pins (6 usable as PWM outputs) and 6 analog inputs.
how_to_use: Connect it to a computer over USB to upload a sketch (program); it then runs that program on its own, reading inputs and driving outputs.

plain.what: The little computer at the heart of most projects. You write a program on your laptop, send it over USB, and the Uno runs it — switching lights, reading buttons and sensors.
plain.how: Plug it into your computer with the USB cable. Wires go into the black sockets along its edges: numbered pins (0–13, A0–A5) for things you control or read, and 5V / GND for power.

pins.GND: ground — the minus (−) side, every circuit needs it
pins.13: a normal on/off pin (also wired to the little built-in light)
pins.A0: reads 'how much' — like a knob's position or a light level
